ai.thread_title: Claude Code accidentally exposes secrets in GitHub repos; credential caching bypassed
ai.name: Anthropic / Builder reports
ai.hook: Claude Code settings files leak API keys, passwords to public GitHub; 1,122+ repos affected.
insights: **Settings files with secrets** exposed when Claude Code commits are merged without credential filtering
Pattern repeats prior 'Don't Ask Again' leak: Claude's **assumption of trust in IDE environment** bypasses secure handling
Affects practitioners shipping agent-generated PRs directly; no widespread credential rotation needed yet, but cleanup underway
ai.for_you: CRITICAL: If you use Claude Code for agency work, audit any commits to your repositories immediately. Add `.env` and settings files to `.gitignore` before running agents. Implement pre-commit hooks to scan for API keys before pushing. This is a blocker for production use of Claude Code in client work until you add guardrails.
ai.what_changed: Earlier thread (Sunday) reported the vulnerability; Ars Technica confirmed 1,122 repos now public. Anthropic has not announced a complete fix.
ai.reason: Direct security risk to your agency's codebase and client data if using Claude Code for development.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Repeating failure mode after prior fix; blocks safe use of Claude Code in production workflows.
